items.title: Kabardinka
items.creator: Nikolai Alexandrovich Yaroshenko
items.notes: "Kabardinka" is an 1880 oil sketch by Realist painter Nikolai Yaroshenko, housed in the Poltava Regional Art Museum. Created during his travels in the Caucasus, the portrait captures a Kabardian woman in traditional Circassian attire, featuring a distinctive cylindrical hat and draped veil.

items.title: Khimsad Loov
items.notes: "Khimsad Loov, an Abazin girl from the Loov family. It was captured between 1870 and 1890 by the photographer Dmitry Ivanovich Yermakov in Kumsko-Loovsky Aul (present-day Krasny Vostok, Karachay-Cherkessia) and is officially registered under master negative plate № 3502. Decades later, the glass negative was acquired by archaeologist and ethnographer Alexander Alexandrovich Miller during his regional field expeditions, leading to its formal indexing and top-stamping into the Ethnographic Department of the Russian Museum of Emperor Alexander III in 1913. Today, this foundational visual record is preserved within the permanent national collections of the Russian Museum of Ethnography in St. Petersburg [ROSPHOTO Works by Tiflis Photographer on the Verge of the ..., ROSPHOTO Writing with Light. Dmitry Yermakov].

items.title: Circassia on a map of the Turkish Empire
items.notes: A copper-engraved map titled Nova Imperii Turcarum Tabula, ad usum Serenissimi Burgundiae Ducis (New Map of the Turkish Empire, for the use of the Most Serene Duke of Burgundy), created by the prominent French cartographer and geographer Alexis-Hubert Jaillot around 1696–1700. It mentions CIRKASI, CIRCASSES, and ABASSA in Caucasus.

items.title: Circassia on a map of the Russian Empire
items.notes: A 1790 antique map by British cartographer Thomas Kitchin depicts the Caucasus, Circassia, and the Black Sea coast. Engraved for publisher Robert Sayer, it translates official charts from the Imperial Academy at St. Petersburg. Featuring distinctive dual scales in geometrical miles and Russian wersts, the map documents late 18th-century borderlines, tribal territories like the "Kuban Tartars," and historic steppe migration zones before the mid-19th-century Caucasian War.

items.title: Cherkes Ethem
items.notes: Cherkes Ethem (1886–1948) was a prominent Circassian guerrilla leader who became a vital militia commander in the early stages of the Turkish War of Independence. Leading the irregular Kuvâ-yi Seyyâre (Mobile Forces), he initially earned national acclaim for stalling the Greek military advance and suppressing internal anti-revolutionary rebellions. However, his independent stance and refusal to merge his forces into the newly established regular Turkish army led to a bitter conflict with the central Ankara government. Declared a traitor and rebel in late 1920, he was defeated and spent the remainder of his life in exile.
